basis: Neurodevelopmental encephalopathy; neonatal central respiratory dysfunction and feeding difficulty do not establish intrinsic lung or gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital cyst of the embryonic thyroid migration tract; endocrine axis reflects developmental origin, without implying thyroid hormone dysfunction.
Defective opsonization is an immune-function disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Isolated congenital impairment of brain growth; neurodevelopmental disorder ancestry supports the neurologic axis.
Ocular refractive and growth disorder causing impaired distance vision.
Malignant circulating plasma cells; lytic skeletal disease occurs in roughly 35-50% and renal impairment in roughly 30-50%.
Fibrous membrane on the retinal surface can distort the macula and impair vision.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis and chronic sinonasal disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 5/5 annotated patients.
Debrancher deficiency defines hepatic and muscle glycogenosis; cardiac hypertrophy occurs in roughly 50-70%. Listed immune/ID frequencies are atypical for GSD III.
Structural skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy occurs in 2/4 annotated patients. Reduced vital capacity alone reflects respiratory muscle weakness.
Neoplasm originates in or occupies the ocular ciliary body.
Progressive cerebellar, brainstem and peripheral nerve degeneration; eye-movement abnormalities are neurologic, while optic atrophy is occasional.
Glycosylation disorder with skeletal dysplasia and anterior-eye defects; hydronephrosis in 1/1 annotated patient supports renal involvement, with uncertain frequency.
Localized corneal stromal inflammation; idiopathic inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability commonly characterize partial trisomy 14q; other structural abnormalities vary across duplication subtypes.
Astrocytic tumour originates in and diffusely infiltrates central nervous system tissue.
Congenital cutaneous hamartoma composed of malformed hair follicles within the dermis.
Acute coronary arterial occlusion causes myocardial infarction; other organ complications are not defining or consistently common.
Immune-complex vascular inflammation; cutaneous small-vessel inflammation affects most patients across the listed subtypes. Renal and gut involvement vary by subtype.
Parathyroid hyperplasia causes primary hyperparathyroidism; chronic skeletal demineralization commonly exceeds 30%. Subtype-specific frequency data are limited.
Defining intellectual disability, ophthalmoplegia with retinal abnormalities, and congenital furrowed tongue; each is annotated as very frequent.
Defining arrhythmia, microcephaly and pigmentation; tooth agenesis 80-99%. Cap excludes strabismus and skeletal maturation delay (30-79%); endocarditis is separate.
Infectious osteomyelitis of the petrous temporal bone; accompanying otitis is a separate infection and does not establish intrinsic inner-ear damage.
Rag nutrient-sensing/metabolic signalling disorder; end-organ disease varies across subtypes. [Review](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-50034-4)
Progressive cerebral arterial stenosis; direct ischemic brain injury with stroke and persistent deficits affects roughly 30-50% in moyamoya, with limited subtype data.
